transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14 15:30 PT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Brightview Head of Platform), Raj (Brightview Security), Nora (Brightview ML), Tom (Brightview Cloud)

Summary (auto): quick recap at end. Some auto-transcript noise, names occasionally mis-transcribed.

00:00 Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, can folks hear me ok?
00:04 Sofia: yep, we can hear you. thanks.
00:06 Ethan: cool so today quick aim—scope the private networking POC and nail down success criteria and timeline. Priya will go over the benchmark plan and then Tom and Raj can cover security/egress notes.
00:20 Priya: hi all, hi, um i'm going to run through the options we typically do: we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and for on-prem customers we can do a customer-provisioned gateway or Transit-GW style peering, so, uh, trade-offs largely are egress+latency vs management complexity.
00:40 Tom: quick q — for peering what's the recommended path for us in our multi-account setup? we use AWS orgs, TGW for intra-account, is peering required or can we use PrivateLink?
00:52 Priya: good q. TL;DR: VPC peering is simplest and gives lowest latency but requires routes and cross-account peering setup; PrivateLink (endpoint services) is easier from an IAM boundary perspective and avoids route table changes but adds a small latency bump and per-GB egress cost differences. For POC we usually do VPC peering for raw perf baselines and then show PrivateLink as the secure managed alternative.
01:15 Raj: from a security standpoint we need to know what egress is permitted. our policy blocks direct internet egress from prod, so the POC must either live in our approved VPC or use PrivateLink so we don't open large outbound ranges. also EU data cannot leave eu-west-1 for certain datasets.
01:35 Priya: noted. we can do region-specific endpoints and pin model serving to eu-west-1 for those datasets. For the peering test we can create a Redwood POC VPC in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 and peer to your dev/test VPCs.
01:50 Nora: workload sizing: for chat assistant flows we'd expect approx 1.2k tokens per session average, peak concurrency 60 sessions, sustained QPS about 8 req/s for the initial pilot, bursting to 20 qps during peaks. we also have a batch embedding job at night, ~= 500M embeddings/month.
02:14 Priya: ok that's super helpful. for the chat flows target p95 <250ms is ambitious but doable with H100-backed Dedicated nodes and optimized batching; with hosted instances you might see p95 in 350-450ms depending on prompt size and concurrency.
02:30 Ethan: just to clarify, are you ok with Redwood running benchmarks in a POC VPC we provision and then sharing token-level cost and latency?
02:40 Sofia: yes, as long as network egress is constrained and the IPs are whitelisted. we can't allow any outbound to third-party endpoints beyond what you provide.
02:50 Priya: we'll provide the IP ranges used during the POC and can work through your security team to reduce them to specific ENIs if needed. Redwood also supports customer-managed KMS for key material for any logs/data at rest.
03:10 Raj: SOC2 and audit logs—do you provide per-request audit logs and encryption in transit?
03:18 Ethan: yes, we provide audit logs, SAML/SSO integration, RBAC and KMS integration. we'll attach SOC2 report and a summary of our logging retention. note: logs can be routed to your S3/CloudWatch in the POC VPC if you prefer.
03:38 Tom: for PrivateLink do you need a NLB on our side or you provide the service endpoint?
03:44 Priya: Redwood exposes the service behind a gateway in the Redwood VPC; for PrivateLink you'll create an interface endpoint in your account that connects to our endpoint service—no need to run an NLB on your side. there is an additional hop which may add ~5-15ms depending on region.
04:05 Nora: about data residency—some PHI-derived metadata must remain in EU; can we set routing so requests with that flag hit eu-west-1 model shard only?
04:15 Priya: yes, request tagging and routing is supported. we can pin model versions and route by policy: customer data residency tags -> eu-serving. fallback rules can be set to reject cross-region fallthrough.
04:30 Ethan: can we talk benchmarks? Priya you had a plan?
04:35 Priya: yep quick sketch: Week 0-1: infra + network set up (VPC peering + whitelisting), Week 2: baseline latency/throughput tests (single model, H100, 1k seq), Week 4: scaling tests (increase concurrency to 100+, run embedding throughput overnight), Week 6: production-like runs and final report with cost per 1k tokens and recommended quantization/instance profile. success criteria: p95 latency <250ms for chat OR documented tradeoffs, embedding throughput >= 1M embeddings/day for the nightly job, and validated egress/no-data-leak checks.
05:10 Sofia: timeline sounds fine. what about endpoints in GCP or Azure? we use GCP for some workloads and would prefer eu-west-1 equivalent region or regional responsibility.
05:24 Priya: currently we have eu-west-1 and us-east-1 deployments; we can replicate to GCP regions for Private installs but for hosted POC we map to the cloud region (AWS). if GCP region is mandatory we can discuss a private deployment option (Redwood Private) which runs in your VPC or on-prem.
05:45 Tom: egress cost question — if we use VPC peering is there still egress charged by AWS between accounts?
05:52 Priya: VPC peering traffic within the same region is typically free for data transfer across AZs? (note: transcript may misstate exact cloud billing) but there are cross-AZ charges sometimes; PrivateLink has per-GB costs and endpoint hour costs. we'll send a cost comparison doc.
06:10 Ethan: also worth noting we can run quantized model variants to reduce instance sizes — that'll change latency and cost. we'll include recommended quantization (int8) for embeddings and a mixed int8/FP16 for chat.
06:25 Nora: for our benchmarks - we'll provide a 50-sample prompt set and a 500-sample long-context set, and we want to see regression in quality <2% against our baseline.
06:38 Priya: ok we'll run both quality and perf; for quality we'll run rouge/bertscore and signal any hallucination rates. that will be part of the Week 6 final.
06:50 Raj: one more security ask — can you support bringing your server certs into our internal PKI and manage mTLS?
06:57 Priya: we do support mTLS termination on PrivateLink and can integrate with customer CAs for on-prem deployments. we'll check for POC applicability.
07:10 Ethan: ok let's capture next steps — we need to provision a POC VPC, exchange IP ranges, Redwood sends security artifacts, and schedule the perf run.
07:22 Sofia: agreed. also we'll need the Redwood SE to provide a small runbook so our cloud team can do the peering with minimal back and forth.
07:30 Priya: i'll draft the runbook and the benchmark plan; Ethan will attach the SOC2 and security summary.
07:36 Tom: for the POC metrics, we'll want token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latencies in the dashboard. is that available in the POC console?
07:44 Liam: yes our console gives per-route model cost and p95/p50 latencies; during POC we can share a temporary dashboard link.
07:52 Sofia: ok perfect. if we hit the p95 target in Week 2 we'll consider a Dedicated reserved footprint; otherwise we'll evaluate Private.
08:00 Ethan: great, we'll follow up with the materials. thanks everyone.
08:05 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-typed cloud billing details, product names like 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes come through as 'Redwood Dedicate'.
